sentences.text: Proceedings in the present arise from filing of DAR in FIR No.282/2016 under section 279/304A IPC & u/s 146/196 M.V. Act registered at PS Farsh Bazar.

Facts in brief are that 27.06.2015 at about 10.15 p.m. deceased Sachin Kadyan was coming on his motorcycle no.DL- 7SBP-6770 (Bajaj Pulsar)
from Karkardooma Court to Vishwas Nagar, in the meanwhile a tractor bearing registration no.UP-12Y-0822 being driven by its driver came from Park Plaza Hotel side at a high speed and in rash and negligent manner and hit the motorcycle of the deceased.
As a result deceased fell on the road along with his motorcycle and sustained severe injuries on his head, shoulder, face, back and other parts of body.
Deceased was taken to Dr.Hedgewar Hospital vide MLC No.2250/2016 and he was referred to GTB Hospital where he succumbed due to accidental injuries on 28.06.2016.
2. It is stated that at the time of accident deceased was plying a taxi and used to earn a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month beside earning Rs.10,000/- per month from tour and travel work.
3. Reply to the DAR has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 in which an objection has been taken that no accident as alleged was caused by the tractor of respondent.

It is stated that at the time of accident R1 was going at a normal speed by his tractor and when he reached at Karkari Road near MCD office, suddenly a motorcycle no.DL-7SBP-6770 came at high speed, rashly and negligently and hit the tractor from left side.
It is stated that R1 is not permanent driver or employee of respondent no.2 Umar Mohmad and R1 was employed for only one day for taking his goods.
4. In its reply filed on behalf of respondent no.2, an objection MACT No.2194/2016 Digitally signed by SHELENDER Page 2 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date:

2024.09.12 17:02:26 +0530 has been taken that R2 sold out vehicle no.UP-12Y-0822 to Sh.Sanjay s/o Hariya Singh on 05.11.2015 for an amount of Rs.3,50,000/- but Sh.Sanjay has not transferred the said vehicle in his name.
It is stated that on 27.06.2016 at about 8.35 p.m. i.e. at the time of occurrence of accident respondent no.1 was driving the above said vehicle from Park Plaza Hotel to Karkardi Road MCD Office.
It is stated that R2 is totally innocent and has not committed any such accident.

5. On the basis of pleadings of parties following issues were framed by my Ld. Predecessor on 28.11.2016 :
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving vehicle bearing no.
UP-12Y-0822 on 27.06.2016 at 10.15 pm near MCD Office, Karkari Road, Vishwas Nagar, Delhi in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hit against motorcycle bearing no.DL-7SBP-6770 as a result its occupant namely Sachin Kadyan sustained fatal injuries?
OPP (2)Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation, if so and for what amount?
OPP (3)Relief.

It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

sentences.text: To prove the manner in which accident occurred petitioners have examined PW3 Ct.Pradeep who has testified that in the night intervening 27.06.2016 and 28.06.2016 he was on night duty as ERV driver.
At about 10.15 p.m. he saw one tractor bearing registration no. UP- 12Y-0822 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, coming from the side of Park Plaza towards MCD office.
PW3 says that said tractor hit a motorcyclist who was on motorcycle no.DL-7S-BP-6770 (Bajal Pulsar) from the side of Karkardooma Courts.
PW3 says that because of accident motorcyclist fell down and sustained injuries, driver of the offending vehicle/tractor was apprehended by PW3 and HC Chander Bhan.
Injured was removed to Dr.Hedgewar Hospital, a call was made at 100 number.

Thus evidence of PW3 coupled with the police case documents including charge sheet,
site plan, mechanical inspection report, seizure memo offending vehicle no. UP-12Y-0822 establish that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 while driving offending vehicle no. UP-12Y-0822.
Issue accordingly decided in favour of the petitioners.
Issue No.2 12. In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by MACT No.2194/2016 Digitally signed Page 6 SHELENDER by SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.09.12 17:02:49 +0530 the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand) The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased 15.
PW1 Bhawna is the wife of deceased Sachin Kadyan and PW2 Attar Singh is father of deceased.
Both these witnesses have testified that at the time of accident deceased was 24 years of age.
Education documents Ex.PW1/2 also proved that date of birth of deceased was 20.11.1992.
As such at the time of accident on 27.06.2016 deceased was 23 years 07 months of age.
Assessment of Income of deceased 16.
As per PW1 and PW2 deceased at the time of accident earning Rs.20,000/- by doing a tour and travel work and taxi business.
PW1 admits in her cross examination that she has not filed any income proof of her late husband, similarly PW2 also admits that he has no documentary evidence of the income of his son.
It has come on the judicial record from the educational documents of deceased Sachin Kadyan that deceased was educated upto senior secondary.
In such circumstance in the absence of any specific proof of income of the deceased, notional income of deceased is taken at parity with matriculate worker in Delhi which is Rs.11,622/- per month.
Application of Multiplier 17.
As held above, deceased was 23 years 07 months of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.

In Para 21 of the judgment, the guidelines for the multiplier were laid down in accordance MACT No.2194/2016 SHELENDER by SHELENDER Page 8 MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.09.12 17:03:02 +0530 with age are as under:

This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

(iv) In case, the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

An addition of 25% where MACT No.2194/2016 Digitally signed by SHELENDER Page 9 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.09.12 17:03:08 +0530 the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

20. Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 23 years 07 months, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 40% of the income of deceased (aged below 40 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.
Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses:
21. After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
Deductions out of earning of the deceased Number of dependents Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent family 1/4th members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent family 1/5th members exceeds 6 (six)

LIABILITY 27.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
Respondent no.1 in the reply has taken the plea that he was only a contractual driver.

Whereas respondent no.2/ registered owner of the tractor has taken the plea that he has already sold the offending vehicle no. UP-12Y-0822 to one Sanjay s/o Hariya Singh for Rs.3,50,000/- on 05.11.2013.
However said Sanjay has not got transferred the said vehicle in his name from concerned transport authority.
28. Both the pleas taken by respondent no.1 and 2 have not been substantiated by leading any evidence.
It is matter of record that three effective opportunities were given to respondents to lead evidence but no evidence was led.
No doubt prior thereto a considerable period was taken on behalf of petitioners for completing PE but fact remains that no evidence at all was led on behalf of respondents.
Therefore the pleas taken by them in their replies have not been proved.
Even otherwise it is matter MACT No.2194/2016

Therefore liability to pay compensation is jointly and severally upon respondent no.1 and 2.

5. On the basis of pleadings of parties following issues were framed by my Ld. Predecessor on 28.11.2016 :
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving vehicle bearing no.
UP-12Y-0822 on 27.06.2016 at 10.15 pm near MCD Office, Karkari Road, Vishwas Nagar, Delhi in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hit against motorcycle bearing no.DL-7SBP-6770 as a result its occupant namely Sachin Kadyan sustained fatal injuries?
OPP (2)Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation, if so and for what amount?
OPP (3)Relief.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
10.
Vehicle was being plied on the road without insurance.
Thus evidence of PW3 coupled with the police case documents including charge sheet,
site plan, mechanical inspection report, seizure memo offending vehicle no. UP-12Y-0822 establish that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 while driving offending vehicle no. UP-12Y-0822.
Issue accordingly decided in favour of the petitioners.
Issue No.2 12. In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
It has come on the judicial record from the educational documents of deceased Sachin Kadyan that deceased was educated upto senior secondary.
In such circumstance in the absence of any specific proof of income of the deceased, notional income of deceased is taken at parity with matriculate worker in Delhi which is Rs.11,622/- per month.
Application of Multiplier 17.
As held above, deceased was 23 years 07 months of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.
20. Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 23 years 07 months, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 40% of the income of deceased (aged below 40 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.
21. After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
Deductions out of earning of the deceased Number of dependents Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent family 1/4th members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent family 1/5th members exceeds 6 (six)
22.
Further, in view of recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 2705 of 2020, decided on 30.06.2020, loss of consortium has to be fixed for each of the LRs.
Petitioner shall also be entitled to interest @ 8% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.

Since, the deceased was survived by four legal heirs, therefore, the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.2,28,000/- (48,000 X 4 + 18,000 + 18,000) under this head.
